desc: Define DP state: set of tuples (altSum, parity, product), initialized with (0, 0, 1) representing empty subsequence; parity 0 means next element would be at even index (added), parity 1 means subtracted.

For each num in nums, extend existing states: newSum = altSum + num if parity==0 else altSum - num; newProduct = product * num (cap/skip if > limit); newParity = 1 - parity. Merge new states into the DP set (keep old states too).
Prune: only keep products ≤ limit; bound altSum range to [-1800, 1800].
After processing all numbers, collect all products from states where altSum == k (any parity, non-empty only).
Return the maximum such product, or -1 if none exist.

Implement grouped DP: count occurrences of each value 0..12; process each distinct value with its count c, trying j = 0..c copies (contribution 0 if j even else ±v; parity flips iff j odd; product *= v^j, special-case v=0 → 0).
Use dict keyed by (sum, parity) → set of products; separate dp2 map tracks non-empty subsequences; empty state (0,0)→{1} seeds new non-empty states each group.
Prune products > limit at every transition; cap sum range to [-1800, 1800].
Final answer: max product in dp2[(k,0)] ∪ dp2[(k,1)]; product 0 is a valid answer distinct from -1.
Clean up and verify: removed dead first transition loop; verified three examples plus edge cases ([0] k=0 → 0; single element over limit → -1; unreachable k → -1; parity flips via zeros/ones).
